concept.name: MFA & Risk-Based Authentication

relationships.description: Connects MFA & Risk-Based Authentication to api security oauth2 in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Risk-based Multi-Factor Authentication (RBA) evaluates contextual telemetry—device posture, ASN/GeoIP, impossible travel, and TLS fingerprints—in real time to dynamically step up high-risk logins to phishing-resistant WebAuthn/FIDO2 while keeping trusted sessions frictionless.
spark.keyTakeaway: Static SMS/push MFA fails against AiTM reverse-proxy phishing and MFA fatigue; pair FIDO2/WebAuthn (origin-bound keys) with a contextual risk engine that challenges only anomalous logins and revokes sessions on mid-session risk spikes.

concept.whyItMatters: Credential stuffing and Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) phishing proxies (like Evilginx) routinely bypass passwords and even TOTP/SMS codes by relaying them in real time, while attackers overwhelm users with push notifications (MFA fatigue) until someone taps Approve. Risk-based authentication combined with origin-bound FIDO2/WebAuthn stops both classes of attack without forcing legitimate users to solve MFA on every page load.
whenToUse: Consumer and enterprise SSO gateways (OIDC / SAML) protecting high-value accounts, admin consoles, or financial transfers.
Reducing login friction for trusted corporate devices (mTLS/MDM-enrolled laptops on corporate VPN) while requiring strong step-up for unknown IPs or new browsers.
Meeting NIST SP 800-63B AAL2/AAL3 or PCI-DSS / SOC2 compliance requirements for phishing-resistant authentication and adaptive session protection.
whenNotToUse: Machine-to-machine (M2M) service accounts—use short-lived OIDC workload identity tokens, SPIFFE/mTLS certificates, or asymmetric JWTs rather than interactive MFA.
Emergency break-glass recovery paths without an offline backup key—locking out all admins because a risk engine flagged a datacenter outage IP can prolong a P0 incident.
Public, unauthenticated read-only endpoints where session state and user identity do not exist.
keyPoints: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2 / WebAuthn / Passkeys) cryptographically binds the signature to the exact TLS `rpId` domain, making AiTM reverse-proxy phishing mathematically impossible.
Risk engines score signals in <50 ms: known device cookie/fingerprint, IP reputation (Tor/VPN/residential proxy ASN), impossible travel (>800 km/h between logins), and JA4 TLS fingerprint.
Push MFA must enforce Number Matching (user types a 2-digit code shown on the login screen) and display app/location context to defeat MFA fatigue bombing.

Authentication Context Class Reference (`acr`) and Authentication Methods References (`amr`) claims in OIDC ID/access tokens let downstream APIs enforce step-up before sensitive actions (e.g., wire transfers).
Continuous Access Evaluation (CAEP / Shared Signals) extends risk checks beyond login time, revoking refresh tokens mid-session if a device loses MDM compliance or changes ASN mid-session.

examples.title: Stopping AiTM Phishing & MFA Fatigue at an Enterprise IdP
examples.scenario: Attackers bought stolen employee credentials, automated 40 push-MFA prompts at 2:00 AM until a fatigued engineer tapped Approve, and harvested session cookies via an Evilginx proxy.
examples.outcome: Enabling FIDO2/WebAuthn hardware keys for engineering/admin roles, enforcing Number Matching on push fallback, and raising the risk score for off-hours logins from residential ASNs eliminated AiTM and fatigue compromises.

examples.title: Adaptive Step-Up for Consumer Banking Transfers
examples.scenario: Forcing TOTP on every login dropped mobile conversion by 14%, yet allowing password-only transfers exposed users to credential-stuffing account takeovers.
examples.outcome: Deploying a risk engine (0–30 allow, 31–70 WebAuthn/TOTP step-up, 71+ block) kept 86% of logins single-tap on known devices while requiring `acr=aal3` step-up for new-device logins and >$1,000 transfers, cutting ATO fraud by 92%.

tradeOffs.factor: FIDO2 / WebAuthn vs. TOTP / SMS OTP
tradeOffs.pro: WebAuthn is origin-bound (immune to AiTM phishing), requires zero shared secrets on the server, and completes in one biometric tap.
tradeOffs.con: Requires cross-device passkey sync (iCloud/Google) or hardware keys (YubiKey) and clear recovery flows if a user loses their primary device.

tradeOffs.factor: Strict Risk Thresholds vs. User Friction
tradeOffs.pro: Aggressive risk scoring blocks VPNs, Tor exit nodes, and new ASNs immediately, minimizing account takeover blast radius.
tradeOffs.con: Legitimate travelers, privacy-conscious VPN users, and mobile CGNAT carriers (where IPs hop cities) suffer false-positive lockouts.

tradeOffs.pro: Failing closed (forcing step-up MFA when the risk service times out) guarantees attackers cannot bypass MFA by DDoSing the risk scorer.
tradeOffs.con: If the risk engine has a 500 ms latency spike or outage, every user gets challenged—or blocked if their MFA channel is also degraded.

failureModes.name: AiTM Reverse-Proxy Session Hijacking
failureModes.description: An attacker hosts `login-corp.evil.com`, proxies traffic to the real IdP, and tricks the user into entering password + TOTP/SMS; the proxy steals the resulting `Set-Cookie` session token.
failureModes.mitigation: Mandate FIDO2/WebAuthn (which verifies `rpId` matches the real origin) and bind session cookies to device keys (DBSC / Token Binding).

failureModes.name: MFA Fatigue (Push Bombing)
failureModes.description: Attacker scripts repeated login attempts with a leaked password, flooding the victim's phone with push prompts until they tap Approve by mistake or annoyance.
failureModes.mitigation: Require Number Matching on all push prompts, rate-limit push requests (e.g., max 3 per 15 min), and lock the account on repeated denials.

failureModes.name: SIM-Swapping & SS7 Interception
failureModes.description: Attackers bribe or socially engineer a mobile carrier to port the victim's phone number to an attacker SIM, intercepting SMS OTPs in minutes.
failureModes.mitigation: Deprecate SMS OTP for high-value accounts in favor of WebAuthn/Passkeys or app-based TOTP (RFC 6238).

failureModes.name: Risk Engine Latency / Fail-Open Bypass
failureModes.description: A slow GeoIP/ML risk model times out at 2 seconds and the auth gateway defaults to `risk=0` (allow), letting credential-stuffing bots slip through unchallenged.
failureModes.mitigation: Keep risk evaluation under 50 ms using local MaxMind MMDB/Redis caches and fail-safe to `step-up MFA` (never `allow`) on timeout.

commonMistakes: Treating SMS OTP or un-numbered Push notifications as equivalent to FIDO2/WebAuthn against targeted phishing.
Checking risk only at `/login` and never re-evaluating `acr`/`amr` or IP/device changes during a 30-day refresh-token lifetime.
Leaving legacy authentication protocols (IMAP, POP3, SMTP basic auth, XML-RPC) enabled, which completely bypass modern OIDC MFA policies.
Allowing unlimited TOTP guesses (`6 digits = 1,000,000` combinations) without strict per-user rate limiting (e.g., 5 attempts per 15 min).
Storing TOTP shared secrets in plaintext in the database instead of encrypting them with an envelope KMS key.

sections.content:
## The idea

Traditional MFA applies a blunt, static rule: ask every user for a second factor on every login, regardless of context. That creates two problems: **friction fatigue** (users blindly tap Approve on push prompts) and **channel vulnerability** (SMS and TOTP codes can be phished by Adversary-in-the-Middle proxies).

**Risk-based authentication (RBA)** separates *session assurance* from *static checklists*. On every authentication or sensitive action, an **Auth Gateway** streams contextual telemetry to a **Risk Scoring Engine** in <50 ms. Low-risk logins from a recognized, healthy device pass silently; medium-risk logins trigger a **phishing-resistant FIDO2/WebAuthn step-up** (cryptographically bound to the exact domain origin); and high-risk logins (impossible travel, known credential-stuffing ASN) are blocked and trigger token revocation.

## Concrete walkthrough

Trace an OIDC login attempt to `auth.example.com` protected by RBA + WebAuthn:

1. **Primary credential & telemetry capture:** User submits username/password (or passkey identifier). The Auth Gateway collects client IP, ASN, MaxMind GeoIP2 coordinates, JA4 TLS fingerprint, and a signed HTTP-only device token.
2. **Sub-50 ms risk scoring:** The Risk Engine checks Redis for recent login locations. Last login was 20 minutes ago in Bengaluru (12.97°N, 77.59°E); this attempt originates from a residential proxy ASN in Frankfurt (50.11°N, 8.68°E)—an impossible travel velocity of ~21,000 km/h. Risk score jumps to `68` (Medium-High).
3. **Phishing-resistant step-up:** Rather than trusting a password or sending an SMS, the gateway generates a 32-byte cryptographic challenge (`WebAuthn AssertionOptions`) with `rpId: "auth.example.com"`.
4. **Origin-bound verification:** The browser's WebAuthn API verifies the TLS origin matches `auth.example.com` (blocking any AiTM proxy on `auth-example.evil.com`), prompts the user's biometric/YubiKey, and returns the ECDSA signature.
5. **Claim issuance:** The gateway verifies the signature against the user's stored public key and issues an OIDC ID Token stamped with `acr: "aal3"` and `amr: ["pwd", "hwk"]`. Downstream payment APIs inspect `acr` before allowing wire transfers.

data.title: Contextual Risk Scoring and Origin-Bound WebAuthn Step-Up

edges.label: 1. Credentials + context
edges.title: Login initiation
edges.description: User submits primary auth along with device cookie, IP, and TLS JA4 fingerprint.

edges.label: 2. Evaluate signals
edges.title: Real-time risk scoring
edges.description: Risk engine checks impossible travel, ASN reputation, and device history against Redis state.

edges.label: 3. Score 68 -> Step-up
edges.title: Adaptive policy decision
edges.description: Score 0-30 allows SSO; 31-70 requires step-up MFA; 71-100 blocks and revokes refresh tokens.

edges.label: 4. Generate 32B challenge
edges.title: Challenge issuance
edges.description: Gateway fetches a fresh random WebAuthn challenge bound strictly to rpId=auth.example.com.

edges.label: 5. Sign with private key
edges.title: Biometric / hardware proof
edges.description: Authenticator signs the challenge + TLS origin; any AiTM proxy domain fails origin validation.

edges.label: 6. Mint token (acr/amr)
edges.title: Session issuance
edges.description: Verified signature mints OIDC tokens stamped with acr=aal3 and amr=[pwd,hwk] for downstream APIs.

data.caption: Risk-based auth keeps trusted logins fast while forcing high-risk sessions through domain-bound WebAuthn verification.

sections.eyebrow: 03 / Factor strength and NIST AAL levels
sections.content:
## Factor strength and NIST AAL levels

Not all second factors defend against the same threat model:

- **SMS / Voice OTP (NIST AAL2 deprecated/restricted):** Vulnerable to SIM swapping, carrier social engineering, and SS7 interception. Avoid for admin or financial accounts.
- **TOTP (RFC 6238, 30 s window) & Number-Matched Push:** Defeats credential stuffing and MFA fatigue, but remains vulnerable to AiTM reverse-proxy phishing because the user manually types or approves a code that a proxy can relay.
- **FIDO2 / WebAuthn & Passkeys (NIST AAL3 when hardware-backed):** Phishing-resistant. The browser includes the exact TLS `origin` in `clientDataJSON`, so an attacker's proxy domain cannot obtain a valid signature for your real domain.

## MFA factor comparison

| Factor Type | AiTM Phishing Resistant | MFA Fatigue Resistant | SIM-Swap Resistant | NIST 800-63B Level | UX Friction |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **SMS OTP** | No | Yes | No | AAL2 (Restricted) | Medium (carrier delays) |
| **TOTP (6-digit)** | No | Yes | Yes | AAL2 | Medium (copy/type code) |
| **Push (Approve/Deny)** | No | No (vulnerable) | Yes | AAL2 (Unsafe alone) | Low (1 tap) |
| **Push + Number Match** | No | Yes | Yes | AAL2 | Low-Medium (type 2 digits) |
| **FIDO2 / WebAuthn** | Yes (Origin-bound) | Yes | Yes | AAL2 / AAL3 | Very Low (1 biometric tap) |

## Failure modes

**1. Account lockout / DoS via bad risk tuning:** Blocking entire mobile carrier ASNs or VPN providers locks out legitimate travelers. Treat high risk as *step-up to WebAuthn* whenever possible, reserving hard blocks for verified credential-stuffing signatures or breached passwords.

**2. Recovery path downgrade:** Requiring a YubiKey to log in is pointless if the "Forgot my security key" flow lets an attacker reset MFA using only an email link or SMS code. Recovery must match or exceed the primary AAL.

**3. Stale session cookies after password reset:** Changing a password or flagging a session as compromised without revoking active refresh tokens and short-lived JWTs (via a Redis revocation list or CAEP event) leaves the attacker logged in.

## Step-up auth and continuous evaluation

Authentication is not a one-time gate at `/login`. Implement **step-up authorization** using OIDC `acr_values` when a user attempts high-impact mutations (changing payout bank details, creating API keys, exporting bulk data) even if they logged in 20 minutes ago.

For long-lived sessions, adopt **Continuous Access Evaluation (CAEP)** patterns: if the user's IP shifts to a new country/ASN mid-session or their corporate MDM device posture flips to non-compliant, invalidate the refresh token immediately and force a fresh WebAuthn assertion.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Prioritize FIDO2 / WebAuthn (Passkeys or hardware keys) as the default second factor for all privileged and high-value accounts.
- [ ] Enable Number Matching and geographic/app context on any legacy Push MFA, and deprecate SMS OTP.
- [ ] Enforce strict rate limiting on TOTP/OTP verification (e.g., max 5 attempts per 15 minutes) and encrypt TOTP seeds at rest.
- [ ] Configure the risk engine to fail-safe to `step-up MFA` (never `allow`) on timeouts, keeping evaluation latency under 50 ms.
- [ ] Disable legacy basic-auth protocols (IMAP/POP3/SMTP auth) and revoke all active refresh tokens on password reset or high-risk anomaly.

simulation.title: Interactive Simulation: Mfa Risk Based Auth

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Risk-based Multi-Factor Authentication (RBA) evaluates contextual telemetry—device posture, ASN/GeoIP, impossible travel, and TLS fingerprints—in real time to dynamically step up high-risk logins to phishing-resistant WebAuthn/FIDO2 while keeping trusted sessions frictionless.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Risk Scoring Engine applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Step-Up Verifier.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Step-Up Verifier experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Mandate FIDO2/WebAuthn (which verifies `rpId` matches the real origin) and bind session cookies to device keys (DBSC / Token Binding).

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Static SMS/push MFA fails against AiTM reverse-proxy phishing and MFA fatigue; pair FIDO2/WebAuthn (origin-bound keys) with a contextual risk engine that challenges only anomalous logins and revokes sessions on mid-session risk spikes.
Avoid trap: Treating SMS OTP or un-numbered Push notifications as equivalent to FIDO2/WebAuthn against targeted phishing.
Avoid trap: Checking risk only at `/login` and never re-evaluating `acr`/`amr` or IP/device changes during a 30-day refresh-token lifetime.
When to reach for it: Consumer and enterprise SSO gateways (OIDC / SAML) protecting high-value accounts, admin consoles, or financial transfers.
When to reach for it: Reducing login friction for trusted corporate devices (mTLS/MDM-enrolled laptops on corporate VPN) while requiring strong step-up for unknown IPs or new browsers.

putItTogether.title: Putting Mfa Risk Based Auth Together
putItTogether.summary: Static SMS/push MFA fails against AiTM reverse-proxy phishing and MFA fatigue; pair FIDO2/WebAuthn (origin-bound keys) with a contextual risk engine that challenges only anomalous logins and revokes sessions on mid-session risk spikes.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Mfa Risk Based Auth before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Enabling FIDO2/WebAuthn hardware keys for engineering/admin roles, enforcing Number Matching on push fallback, and raising the risk score for off-hours logins from residential ASNs eliminated AiTM and fatigue compromises.
